page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores running at 2.5 GHz. The processor includes a 33 MB L3 cache and supports hardware-assisted virtualization alongside instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, AES, and FMA. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.se1.2xlarge delivers modest compute capabilities. In stress-ng and Geekbench tests, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% tier. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in Passmark CPU tests and large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks, achieving 39.75 GB/sec for read operations and 36.51 GB/sec for write operations. Conversely, small-block cached memory bandwidth and database operations, such as Redis SET, rank in the lower 25% tier. LLM inference speeds are average for small 135M models but drop to poor levels for larger 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1.2xlarge offers a high-density memory configuration relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive CPU processing. Due to the lack of local storage and lower single-core performance, it is best suited for memory-intensive applications relying on network-attached storage, such as caching layers, medium-sized databases, and general-purpose memory-optimized workloads.
